events.title: Ìomhar Dearg wants a green axe for use, not for a grave
events.body: At a wake in the north-west, Ìomhar Dearg turns over the dead man's green axe before it goes under the turf and asks the son, plainly, for one of his own to carry and use, having buried enough kin himself to want a tool that earns its keep before it earns its grave.

events.title: The cutters of Àth àrsaidh turn Ìomhar away
events.body: An old cutter at the quarry tells Ìomhar Dearg that no green axe was ever cut to be swung, only shown, and that a man wanting an edge for work should go to a common smith and leave the green stone to the graves it is already promised to.

events.title: Ìomhar's grey axe outlives forty years of use
events.body: Ìomhar Dearg has a common smith cut him a plain grey axe that same winter, and uses it, reground more than once, for the better part of forty years before the head cracks on a misjudged root and he buries it himself in the ground it first turned.

events.title: The last cutter of Àth àrsaidh dies without an apprentice
events.body: The seam of true green stone runs thin under every cut the households of Àth àrsaidh try, and the last cutter who still holds the old skill dies that year with no apprentice behind him, his own sons having gone to herding rather than a stone that no longer pays for the teaching.

events.title: The oak-groves of the north shrink to the sheltered valleys
events.body: About Doire ghlas and the low ground north of it, heather, birch and bog-moss spread over ground the oak had held unchallenged for longer than any household's reckoning, and the groves that gave the north its many doire-names draw back to valleys the wind cannot reach.

events.title: Stepping-stones cross Abhainn fhionn dry-shod
events.body: A household below the willow flats lays flat stones across the shallowest bend of Abhainn fhionn one summer's low water at a time, until within two generations a man may cross the whole width stone to stone in every season but true flood, the first made river-crossing the island has seen.

events.title: Twelve are taken at the fords of Abhainn chaol
events.body: A spate with no warning a slower rise would have given takes a party of twelve crossing with salt at the fords of Abhainn chaol; five bodies go to their own kin, four unclaimed to the nearest household willing to dig, and three are never found.

events.title: Ìomhar comes two days too late to the drowning
events.body: Word reaches Ìomhar Dearg two days' walk south of Abhainn chaol and he comes as fast as the road allows, arriving to a river already fallen back to its ordinary height and the households of both banks already burying what could be found; no household crosses those fords in the wet season after.

events.title: Niall is born to Raonaid on the eastern shore
events.body: Raonaid nic Ailein bears a son on the eastern shore in a colder autumn than the last three running; her half-brother Ìomhar Dearg finds more of her quickness than of his own long line in the child's first evening.

events.title: Ceann chiar cuts two-and-twenty marks for A' Ghaoth Dhubh
events.body: Rebuilding after A' Ghaoth Dhubh that scattered their roofs a generation before, the households of Ceann chiar set a stone in their new-laid houses and cut a plain stroke for every house the wind took, two-and-twenty marks in a row with no names beside them.

events.title: A dry summer is answered by the shared surplus
events.body: The rivers of the eastern plain run so low one summer that Dùn ìseal and Muileann bhàn drive their cattle to Fuarain Theth Muileann ruadh to drink; the surplus each household had kept against such a year holds long enough that no death is counted for the thirst of it.

events.title: A lesser wave comes in at Cnoc chaol
events.body: The sea rises again over the low ground at Cnoc chaol, less far than the wave the coast still tells of; the new houses built higher on the slope since that first wave take no loss, the water finding only empty byres to carry off.

events.title: The crack at Gleann na Scoltaidh moves again
events.body: The old crack in the ground shifts once more, moving the spring back uphill and breaking the line of white stones that marks the danger in two places; the households walk out with fresh stone and lay the line again exactly as their grandmothers laid it the first time.

events.title: Dùghall born to Ìomhar Dearg
events.body: A son is born to Ìomhar Dearg and named Dùghall, a grave, red-haired child with none of his cousin Niall's laughter in him; Ìomhar, near seven hundred years old, carries him on his wanderings before the boy can walk.

events.title: Households settle at Cnoc bheag with no door facing the stone
events.body: A generation settles on the bank of Abhainn ìseal a short walk from the standing stone at Cnoc bheag, and sets its houses, by no law anyone can name, so that no door among them faces the stone; every household built after keeps the same pattern unquestioned.

events.title: Inis bhàn settles the seal-rocks by the tally of the turn
events.body: The households by the seal-rocks off the river mouth at Inis bhàn take one rock to a household in its own turn, kept on notched sticks; a rock taken out of turn is the coast's commonest quarrel, settled always by counting the tally aloud rather than raised voices.

events.title: Ìomhar Dearg asks the king for ground of his own
events.body: Nearly eight hundred years into a wandering right that let him sit at any hearth on the island, Ìomhar Dearg asks the king, on the hill, for ground held in his own name rather than his blood's, wanting a piece of earth that answers to him before it answers to anyone else.

events.title: The king gives Ìomhar the river-grazing of the eastern marches
events.body: The king grants Ìomhar Dearg thin-soiled river-grazing between the last settled households and the open country to the east, telling him only that a share given is a share that can be taken back, as every share on the island has been and will go on being.

events.title: Ìomhar stands on his own ground looking east
events.body: At the day's end Ìomhar Dearg stands alone on the eastern river-grazing, thin grass under his own feet for the first time in nearly eight centuries of walking ground that answered to another name, and looks east toward country he has not yet walked.

events.title: Achadh mhòr's wide field is cleared under Fuarain Theth Muileann ruadh
events.body: A household near Fuarain Theth Muileann ruadh clears and banks the widest single field the eastern country has yet cut from the rough, laying its bank on the stones of an older wall whose builders none of them can name, and grows in a good year wheat enough for three households where before there had been land for none.

events.title: An Cnoc Ruadh's boats come to be kept at Baile ghlas
events.body: Boats drawn up in stone and turf sheds at Baile ghlas along the lake shore come, within a generation, to put out oftener than An Cnoc Ruadh's own strand, so that the harbour built beside the hill grows quietly into the hill's chief fishing ground.

events.title: Achadh naomh fences its spring before it raises a house
events.body: Settlers at Achadh naomh lead a spring round in channels of their own digging and fence it before a single wall is raised, so that a stranger coming on the place first might take the water, and not the people, for what had been settled there.

events.title: Two households at Caol shean give their disputed landing to no one
events.body: Rather than let a quarrel over a stretch of river landing run on with no keeper near enough to draw a lot on it, two households of Caol shean sit out a night together and give the ground to the landing itself, for whoever has a boat drawn up there and no other claim; the households are, within two generations, thoroughly mixed by marriage.

events.title: Catrìona born of the king's blood
events.body: A daughter of the king's blood is born in the valleys under the hill and named Catrìona; before she is ten she can give a household's line back seven names, and the hill begins to watch her as a valley watches a child who does an ordinary thing early.

events.title: Ailis is born east of the vein
events.body: A girl named Ailis is born at what will become Dùn dhearg, into a household already turf-cutting for the fort's first bank, and grows up along the ditch's edge hearing, at her own hearth, tellings of a king beyond the vein who does not grow old.

events.title: A trader tells Ailis of the gate at Dùn ìseal
events.body: A cloth-trader passing through Caol shean's landing tells the children at a hearth of standing at the very gate of Dùn ìseal and seeing a young-faced man come in at it who has held that hill, by every account at the gate, since before its walls were built; the child Ailis asks whether it does not frighten his own children to grow old beside him, and gets no clear answer.

events.title: The households east of the vein raise the double bank at Dùn dhearg
events.body: Owing nothing to Dùn ìseal and asking leave of no one, the households of the eastern country dig a deep ditch and raise a double bank at Dùn dhearg, sharing out the labour and afterward the ground within it by households and not by standing, so that the fort itself sets, without any law behind it, the custom the country keeps from then on.

events.title: A holdout household is left outside Dùn dhearg's second bank
events.body: A family that refuses to send hands to the digging is simply left with its grazing outside the second bank when the ground is drawn, and asks within a generation, of its own accord and under no compulsion, to be let in on the same terms as its neighbours, its late hands reckoned at somewhat less than hands sent early.

events.title: Gille-Brìde's father born in Na Glinn Àrda
events.body: A son is born in Na Glinn Àrda to a household of Somhairle's line, which keeps Sloinneadh a' Chlachair and takes no share; he will live three hundred and eight years, fewer than his own father, and father Gille-Brìde.

events.title: Ruairidh born to Dùghall Dearg
events.body: A son is born to Dùghall Dearg, son of Ìomhar Dearg, and named Ruairidh, grey-eyed like his great-grandfather the king; Ìomhar holds him at his naming and says the boy will outlive the river-grazing and most of what stands on it.

events.title: Ailis's husband is buried on the slope above Dùn dhearg
events.body: The net-mender of Caol shean whom Ailis married in her twenty-second year dies at Dùn dhearg an old man by any island's reckoning, and is carried out and laid on the slope above the houses with his own net-needle set in the ground at his feet.

events.title: Seumas born on An Cnoc Ruadh
events.body: A son is born in An Cnoc Ruadh's hall and named Seumas; the reciters of the lake shore mark his birth in the roll as they have marked every holder's since Beathag Ruadh.

events.title: Ailis sets out for the ford with seal-skins
events.body: In her eighty-first year Ailis of Dùn dhearg carries three winters' store of seal-skins the length of the island toward Cruinneachadh an Àtha, meaning to trade them for salt and to stand in the river of the old tellings before her legs fail her; six of that country go with her, the first of Dùn dhearg's people to make the journey.

events.title: The east reaches the ford after five days on the road
events.body: Ailis's party finds households along the road who have never heard of the country east of the vein, and sleeps a night with a family whose grandfather claims a telling, four hands removed, of An Cruinneachadh Mòr held in the three-thousandth year of the Grove; by the fourth day they walk unremarked among a general traffic of salt- and wool-carriers bound the same way.

events.title: Ìomhar Dearg names the east 'the short-lived' at the ford
events.body: At the fire where Catrìona hears Ailis out, Ìomhar Dearg, holding river-grazing nearby, asks carelessly why ground should be troubled over for people who will all be dead within one of his own lifetimes, and calls them, in that breath, the short-lived; Ailis answers that she has five days' walking behind her and no wish to spend any of what time she has left arguing with a man who will have five centuries to be sorry in.

events.title: Young Catrìona gives Dùn dhearg ground at the ford
events.body: Catrìona, of the king's blood and not yet two hundred and twenty-five years old, hears Ailis of Dùn dhearg out at the ford, asks after the double bank and whether it answers to anyone, and gives the eastern households ground of their own on the far bank, this year and every year after, asking no oath in return and receiving none.

events.title: Salt is carried home to Dùn dhearg without any oath given
events.body: Ailis's party trades its seal-skins for salt enough to see three households through a hard winter and walks home east of the vein without having sworn anything to the ford or to the hill, and the elders of Dùn dhearg agree, hearing it told, that ground held and no word owed for the holding suits them exactly as it stands.

events.title: Ailis dies on the slope above the double bank
events.body: Ailis dies at eighty-five in her own house on the eastern slope of Dùn dhearg's bank, three years after her one journey to the ford, and is buried beside her husband; her grandchildren keep the tale of the seal-skins and the woman of the king's blood who asked nothing back for the ground she gave.

events.title: The ford of the wild cattle is settled at Àth fhiadhaich
events.body: A household settles a stony crossing in the south-eastern hills where wild cattle come down to drink, and rears the calves born on the near bank apart from the wild herd until, within three generations, that ford's cattle are spoken of the length of the coast as the best in the hills.

events.title: Households build about the old landing at Ceann àrsaidh
events.body: People out of An Cnoc Ruadh's country find an old river landing on the Abhainn fhionn, stones set for a boat's keel by hands none living can name, and build their houses about it, naming the place for what they found.

events.title: Inis mhòr's two facing rows are raised
events.body: Households settle Inis mhòr on the Abhainn ghorm and build their houses in two rows facing each other across a single trodden way, so that a neighbour's fire may be borrowed without crossing open ground in the rain; it is the oldest street any teller remembers on Dia-thìr.

events.title: Catrìona takes the hill of Dùn ìseal
events.body: Catrìona, of the king's blood and two hundred and forty-seven years old, takes Dùn ìseal formally as the twelfth to hold it of Rìghrean na Cloiche' line, known already for a memory that can give any household's line back seven names without pausing to think.

events.title: Seumas Òg takes An Cnoc Ruadh
events.body: A young man of seven-and-twenty named Seumas takes up the holding of An Cnoc Ruadh his own line has kept since the palisade first burned, the same season Catrìona takes Dùn ìseal; his name will be the last An Cnoc Ruadh's own spoken roll carries.

events.title: The two rolls are spoken whole at the ford in one night
events.body: Eòin gives the whole roll of Rìghrean na Cloiche from Ailean Mòr to Catrìona's own name, and Ùna gives the whole roll of An Cnoc Ruadh from Beathag Ruadh to Seumas Òg's, from dusk to the grey before morning; it is the first time either roll is heard whole, and those nearest the king see him smile when his own name is spoken.

events.title: The lot for the slab is drawn from every part of the hills
events.body: Where the lot for the keeper of the slab was once drawn only from households near the crack, it comes in these years to be drawn from every part of the hills alike, and Tobar dhìreach becomes a place walked to for its own sake by households whose grandparents never heard the crack mentioned.

events.title: A nameless hand recuts Calbh Cnoc ghorm
events.body: A hand from Catrìona's own hill goes out to Calbh Cnoc ghorm and recuts its worn grooves along their old lines before the rain can lose them; some who come after hold that a single stroke changed in the recutting, though none can agree which, or prove any changed at all.

events.title: Luchd-faire na Lice settle at nine
events.body: The keepers settle at nine, one drawn by lot for each of nine districts of the hills that no household has ever marked on the ground but every household somehow knows the edge of; the nine meet at the slab only when one of their number dies.

events.title: The handful comes to be burned all at once by agreement
events.body: Without any lot or law behind it, every household in reach of another comes to burn its measured handful of an gual dathach on the same dark night, each watching for the first low flame on the nearest hill before lighting its own; the night comes to be called Oidhche na Glaice.

events.title: Cnoc na Claise's household refuses its handful
events.body: The descendants of Torcall Tochlair, who stayed by the trench where his brother was crushed, will not burn the handful with the rest of the hills and give no single answer twice for it; Catrìona sends no one to compel them, and none at the slab asks her to.

events.title: The cord of Dùn ìseal grows to nine hundred knots
events.body: Finding she can no longer carry the whole tally of households in her own head, Catrìona sets her people to counting them plainly on a knotted cord, a knot to a hearth, which grows through her years of holding to some nine hundred knots, the largest count made on Dia-thìr in the age; the king's own kin are never upon it.

events.title: The tally stones of Seann Dunn are set back in their old order
events.body: A family digging a house-floor into an old midden at Seann Dunn strikes a row of upright stones each cut with a single stroke, knows them for the tally stones of the coast's old people, and sets them back as they lay rather than break them for the floor, building further along the midden's shoulder instead.

events.title: The south-eastern coast rows its dead to Eilean ìseal
events.body: The custom grows along the south-eastern coast of rowing the newly dead out to Eilean ìseal rather than burying them on the mainland shore, whether learned from the old coast people's graves across the strait or come to of itself; the tellings let the question stand unsettled.

events.title: Eilean chrom stays unfished
events.body: No household puts out a boat to fish the waters of Eilean chrom, where Gilleasbuig Beag was left with no boat to come back in; his fire was seen three nights running the first year and then no more, and the island stays empty and unfished.

events.title: The nine keepers ask Catrìona to declare their charge
events.body: The nine of Luchd-faire na Lice come up together at the ford and ask Catrìona, then in her twenty-ninth year of holding, to declare their charge over the slab, the lot and the handful before the whole gathering so that no king after her may reach for it as Calum Ciar once did; she names the eldest of them by his own line before he finishes bowing.

events.title: Catrìona answers the keepers: not this year, ask me again
events.body: Catrìona gives the nine keepers neither refusal nor consent, telling them only, "Not this year," and then, before the eldest can press her further, "Ask me again"; the nine go back to their own fires by the slab to wait.

events.title: Eòin Beul-binn and Ùna Ruadh die within two years of each other
events.body: Eòin, whose voice carried the whole roll of Rìghrean na Cloiche across one night at the ford, dies in his eightieth year, and Ùna, who answered him roll for roll for An Cnoc Ruadh, follows him within two years in her seventy-third; the telling of that single night passes from then on at second hand.

events.title: Catrìona falls ill on the hill
events.body: In her two hundred and eighty-ninth year the sickness comes on Catrìona that will not leave again; she keeps her seat at Dùn ìseal as long as she is able, still able to give a household's whole line back seven names, and the nine keepers, hearing of it, send no word asking again.

events.title: Seumas Òg dies on An Cnoc Ruadh
events.body: Seumas Òg, the last name An Cnoc Ruadh's spoken roll carries, dies in his seventy-first year in the winter before Catrìona Mhòr, and the lake shore keeps no holder's fire for him after, only its own.

events.title: The king's kin bring their claims to the hill
events.body: After Catrìona Mhòr's death every soul of the king's blood within three days' walk comes to Dùn ìseal to press a claim on the hill, each able to say the two names of a line whose second name is always Ailean's; the king hears every claim with the same still face.
